Section-11.4 conflict
Direct observation

The current card explicitly describes the census as a “Pre-model A/RECON action-relevance gate.” It executes before any learner, optimizer, or training dataset exists and returns HOST_NOT_DURATION_DISCRIMINATING without creating a model when its conditions fail. The nominal B object can therefore terminate with zero learner updates and zero learner evaluations.

That directly conflicts with the controlling rules:

A B algorithm experiment must exercise the real environment, policy, learner, trainer, and evaluator and report nonzero transition, update, and evaluation counts.

Section 11.4 permits only four B-launch holds: common integrity requirements, the real/nonzero learner path, mandatory resource admission, and the machine-generated exposure line.

Nothing else may hold a B launch.

The engineering-scope specification independently states that the allowable launch conditions are exactly those four and that an additional gate is deleted rather than retained.

The engineering dissent therefore validly reopened this direction node. Repository authority expressly permits a committed engineering dissent to reopen a Pro node and makes evidence-spec section 11 controlling over stronger direction-local B obligations.

Why not run the full B unconditionally

RUN_FULL_B_WITH_NON_GATING_CENSUS could be made formally compliant by deleting the census’s launch authority and forcing all D6 and D8 learner runs to execute. It is not the smallest decision-relevant correction.

If the census finds zero oracle-to-worst span, the denominator is zero. If the span is positive but no state has a material cross-duration preference, the duration-competence predicate can be tied or scientifically vacuous: the models may differ predictively without changing a competent duration choice or native return. Making such cases finite would require material changes to regret, competence, and the result rule, not merely deletion of the early return.

More importantly, the census is the cheaper experiment that determines whether the declared finite host contains the native cross-duration action opportunity needed by the D6 question. The evidence specification prefers an exact census when it is the cheapest decision-relevant discriminator; it prohibits only ritual prerequisites that cannot change the decision. Here the census can change the direction-tier decision: two-sided duration relevance can justify considering a learner comparison, whereas zero or one-sided opportunity calls for a different population or a park assessment.

The class-correct response is therefore to expose that decision as a separate A result—not conceal it as a fifth B-launch gate.

Why not park D6 now

A finite and decision-relevant A object is already fully specifiable from the frozen host, source law, action catalogue, endpoint, and tape count. The defect is methodological, not evidence that D6 is structurally impossible or scientifically valueless.

The accepted D6 mechanism remains distinct: one duration-conditioned head shares value learning across k, while the same-information D8 comparator uses duration-specific heads that do not share. The eventual scientific observable remains competent composite-action selection and native return, not prediction accuracy in isolation.

PARK_D6 is therefore not supported at this boundary.

Evidence assessment
Direct observations

Section 11.4 permits only four B-launch holds and rejects every additional capacity, formal-analysis, prospective-contract, or similar condition as launch authority.

The current card stops before model creation when the 1,152-mission census fails.

The engineering implementation candidate reproduces that early refusal, and no part of the object has been executed.

The current card’s regret denominator and duration-competence criterion are defined using the census’s oracle-value table.

The previously archived Pro response admitted the census inside the B object, which is the exact formulation now reopened; it supplied no subsequent execution evidence.

The accepted direction history keeps B01 stopped and identifies D6/D8 value sharing as the independent mechanism under consideration.

Inference

Separating the census is preferable to unconditional B execution because it answers whether the native decision problem required by the learner comparison exists at all. A failing or one-sided result would otherwise force a full learner study whose principal action-linked estimand is undefined or unable to identify cross-duration value sharing.

This split is not a disguised B gate because:

the present B card is withdrawn from launch;

the A object produces only an A result;

no future B is authorized;

the direction node must reconvene after A;

any later B is a separately named, transparently sequential study and cannot stop on the A result.

Residual uncertainty

The evidence does not show whether the declared host/population will produce:

two-sided material duration relevance;

one-sided duration relevance;

action relevance without material duration preference; or

zero action-value span.

No corresponding census has run.

Even if A later supports a B study and that study favors D6, the strongest alternative remains that the result comes from ordinary lower-dimensional regularization or easier optimization rather than meaningful duration structure. Conversely, heterogeneous state-by-duration values may create negative transfer and favor D8. The existing card expressly preserves this alternative.

Strongest support and contradiction

Strongest support: The current object already contains a fully specified, explicitly A-labelled, 1,152-mission native-return census, and the controlling specification unequivocally prohibits it from stopping a B launch. Because no command has run, separating it preserves every observation and requires no result reinterpretation.

Strongest contradiction: The census was introduced for a legitimate scientific reason: the proposed B action-regret and competence measurements are meaningful only when the host contains cross-duration native action opportunity. Splitting it postpones the real learner experiment and makes any later B transparently outcome-informed. That cost does not reverse the decision because A/B adaptation is permitted, whereas retaining the census as a fifth B-launch hold is expressly prohibited.

If not, does the observed A branch justify one prospectively different host or source-population object, or should D6 be parked?

No answer to that later question is precommitted here.

Finite claim ceiling

This decision establishes only:

The current D6 B card is section-11-incompatible because its finite census is an unauthorized pre-learner B-launch hold, and the smallest legal next object is a separate finite A/RECON duration-action-relevance census.

A positive A branch could establish only finite host/population/action relevance on the exact six states and sixteen tapes per state. It could not establish D6 value, D8 inferiority, cross-k sharing benefit, or B launch authorization.

An adverse A branch could reject only the exact host/source/population/action panel as a useful substrate for the proposed action-linked D6 question. It could not refute D6 on another population or host.
